briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. I will now begin today's climate briefing for September 19, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Global Climate Crisis: A Warning That Has Already Become Reality
sections.content: News collected today clearly demonstrates that the climate crisis is no longer a distant threat but an emergency that has already become reality. According to reports, 'the climate crisis is not the future but a reality that has already begun' [4], and a major catastrophe occurred in the Himalayas, with 1,300 deaths and 5,000 missing [6]. Europe also experienced a 'summer of truth' with record heatwaves, forest fires, and the depletion of rivers and reservoirs, resulting in approximately 35,000 deaths and 180 billion euros in damages [29]. Domestically, facing an 'infinite loop of heavy rains and heatwaves,' there have been calls to transform the national framework towards 'adaptive disaster response' [7], and even in daily life, the impacts of climate change are being felt, such as the unusually high alcohol content in champagne this year [2]. The flood situation in Nepal [25] and the anticipated risk of floods due to winter storms and heavy rains in the UK [28] also warn that climate change is a reality that will affect everyone [23], and the news that even efforts to restore endangered salmon in Maine face uncertain success due to the changing climate clearly reveals the widespread impacts of the climate crisis [22].

sections.title: 🌱 Acceleration of Domestic Renewable Energy Transition and Carbon Neutrality Practices
sections.content: Amidst this crisis, positive movements for renewable energy transition and carbon neutrality practices are actively continuing domestically. The government has activated an inter-ministerial task force (TF) to achieve the '100GW renewable energy' target, closely managing large-scale solar power projects [10], and specific projects are being promoted, such as the public tender for leading developers of a 30MW ground-mounted solar power project in the Saemangeum Smart Green Industrial Complex [20]. At the local government level, Pohang City signed an MOU for RE100 new and renewable energy installation projects in public parking lots [12], and North Chungcheong Province announced an innovative plan to promote a 2.3 trillion won eco-friendly data center that cools AI servers using water from Daecheong Dam [21]. Furthermore, the development of climate-adaptive agricultural technologies is active, with the debut of 'Chungbuk No. 1,' a new variety of white rice resistant to extreme weather [5], and efforts for carbon neutrality are becoming visible in various sectors, such as Gyeonggi Province's blue carbon ordinance, which utilizes coastal ecological resources as assets for carbon neutrality, passing the plenary session [9]. The Saemaul Undong Credit Cooperatives also contributed 2 billion won in social solidarity finance to support renewable energy and social housing projects, expanding the participation of the financial sector [18].

sections.title: 🌍 Strengthening International Cooperation and Expanding Global Climate Response
sections.content: Responses to the climate crisis are being further strengthened through international cooperation that transcends borders. South Korea has signed a climate cooperation MOU with Kyrgyzstan to identify joint projects for renewable energy and carbon reduction, officially commencing 'commercialization' [3, 11], and the Governor of Jeju Province met with the Chinese Ambassador to Korea to discuss new and renewable energy cooperation, expanding the scope of bilateral cooperation [14]. Efforts to support the renewable energy transition in developing countries are also active, with Bangladesh agreeing to provide 169 billion won in low-interest financing for renewable energy projects, including rooftop solar [15]. India's Prime Minister shared India's approach to combating climate change by combining ancient wisdom and clean energy [27], and efforts to raise awareness in the international community are continuing, such as the publication of a new booklet in Canada to help citizens trust climate change information [26].

sections.title: 📰 Climate Change Emerges as a Society-Wide Agenda
sections.content: Climate change has now established itself as a major agenda item across society, beyond specific sectors, and is being discussed in various ways. Domestically, climate discourse is expanding in daily life, with discussions about climate change taking place over traditional tea at Gwangju Hyanggyo [1], and voluntary participation from civil society continues, such as the Yeosu City Mobility Support Center for the Transportation Disadvantaged and the Carbon Neutrality Practice Alliance volunteering at facilities for people with disabilities [8]. Internationally, the climate crisis and AI have become central to political discussions, emerging as one of the key issues in the U.S. midterm elections [24]. This indicates that climate change is a complex challenge affecting all areas, including economy, society, and politics, beyond being a simple environmental issue, demonstrating that society-wide attention and response are essential.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has confronted the reality of the climate crisis while also highlighting proactive response efforts and the expansion of social discourse both domestically and internationally. Through sustained attention and action, we must build a better future. This concludes today's climate briefing.

articles.description: After summer’s heatwaves, prepare for winter of storms and heavy rain, with millions of UK homes at risk of flooding The accelerating climate crisis and this year’s record-breaking El Niño mean that, although the summer’s heatwaves are still fresh in the memory, households in the UK are already being told to prepare for a potentially destructive winter of storms and heavy rain – leaving millions of homes at risk of flooding.Government action is needed to improve flood defences and build reliance

summary.phenomenon: Following this summer's record-breaking heatwaves, the UK anticipates a winter of storms and heavy rain, leaving millions of homes at risk of flooding.
summary.cause: The accelerating climate crisis and this year's record-breaking El Niño phenomenon have been identified as contributing factors to these winter storms and heavy rainfall.
summary.outlook: The government is urged to take action to improve flood defenses and build resilience.

articles.title: Burning forests, emptying rivers, €180bn in damage: Europe’s politicians face reckoning after ‘summer of truth’
articles.description: Amid record-shattering heatwaves and popular demand for climate action, why are politicians often timid or in denial?It was, according to the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, the “summer of truth”. summary.phenomenon: Europe and the Northern Hemisphere experienced climate chaos, including record-breaking heatwaves, crop damage, forest fires, depletion of rivers and reservoirs, warped train tracks, melted roads, and approximately 35,000 deaths in Europe alone, resulting in an estimated 180 billion euros in damages.
summary.outlook: The President of the European Commission described this as the "summer of truth," and despite public demand for climate action, politicians often exhibit a timid or denialist stance, underscoring the need for political accountability.
